textoCompleto: One hot afternoon, a hungry fox was walking through a vineyard. He had been looking for food all day but had found nothing. He was very hungry. Then, he saw something wonderful. A bunch of big, purple, juicy grapes was hanging from a high vine. The grapes looked delicious. 'Oh, those grapes look so good! I must have them!' said the fox. The fox tried to reach the grapes. He stood on his back legs and stretched his paws as high as he could. But the grapes were too high. He could not reach them. The fox decided to try jumping. He took a few steps back, ran forward, and leaped into the air. He almost reached the grapes, but not quite. He tried again. And again. And again. Each time, he jumped higher and higher. But the grapes were always just out of reach. The fox was tired and frustrated. He sat down and looked at the grapes. Finally, he stood up and said, 'Those grapes are probably sour. They would not taste good anyway.' Then he walked away. A bird who had seen everything said, 'You only say the grapes are sour because you cannot reach them.' And that is where the expression 'sour grapes' comes from. It means pretending not to want something just because you cannot have it.
